lineEditor.dragArea: Drag over the frame to mark the analysis area
lineEditor.dragLine: Click and drag over the frame to draw a line
lineEditor.linesIntro: One per bike lane or traffic lane, at any angle. Whoever crosses it is counted; A→B and B→A are the directions. With no lines, every relevant trajectory becomes a candidate.
lineEditor.howToPlaceText: The crossing uses the point where the object touches the ground (bottom of its box): the line should cross only the lane you want, without touching the neighboring ones. Turn off the categories a line does not count (e.g. cars on the bike lane) — they reach the review already proposed as discarded.
lineEditor.useCameraLines: Use the saved lines of a camera
lineEditor.useArea: Analyze only part of the frame
lineEditor.areaIntro: For high cameras or distant objects: the app looks for objects only inside the area, with the full sharpness of the original video — small cyclists that would go unnoticed start being detected. The final video still shows the whole frame.
lineEditor.fitToLinesHint: Goes back to the automatic area, around the lines
lineEditor.areaNoLines: Draw the lines — the area fits around them — or mark it yourself.
lineEditor.areaTooWide: The area is wider than {max} px: the video is downscaled and small objects lose sharpness. A smaller area helps.
lineEditor.lineOutsideArea: The line “{name}” goes outside the analysis area: nothing is detected outside it.
lineEditor.saveAsCamera: Save these lines as a camera

language.label: Language
language.hint: The suggestions from the artificial intelligence and the labels of the final video also come in this language (for videos processed from now on).

help.title: Help and diagnostics
help.text: If something goes wrong, save the diagnostic report and send the file to whoever supports the app. It gathers the program's log, the settings and what happened with each video — without the videos and without your artificial intelligence key.

tech.modelsHint: The first one is the main one; the others step in if it fails (OPENROUTER_MODEL and OPENROUTER_FALLBACK_MODELS in the configuration file)

gpu.title: Graphics card
gpu.apple: This Mac uses the Apple chip to speed up detection automatically. There is nothing to choose.
gpu.noNvidia: We did not find an NVIDIA graphics card in this computer.
gpu.noNvidiaHint: Everything still works, using the processor — but detection takes much longer (a 1-hour video can take a few hours). If you install an NVIDIA card later, come back to Settings.
gpu.useGpuHint: Recommended. Detection becomes several times faster.
gpu.useCpuHint: Much slower. Choose this only if the graphics card causes problems.

engine.title: Detection engine
engine.installTime: It can take 5 to 20 minutes, depending on the internet. Leave the app open; you can go on with the other steps meanwhile.
engine.quickFix: A quick fix to the engine installed by an earlier version of the app. Takes a minute or two.
engine.notInstalled: The detection engine is not installed yet.
engine.notInstalledHint: It is the part that recognizes cyclists, pedestrians and vehicles in the videos. The app downloads and installs everything by itself (it takes about {size} of disk space).
engine.gpuMismatch: The installed engine is not using the graphics card. Reinstall it to take advantage of the card.
engine.systemPython: In this installation the engine is the system Python: install the dependencies from requirements.txt.

key.title: Artificial intelligence (OpenRouter)
key.intro: The app uses an artificial intelligence to suggest what each object is (cyclist, pedestrian, car…) before you confirm. It is a pay-per-use service, OpenRouter: each suggestion costs a fraction of a cent — US$ 5 of credit covers tens of thousands of suggestions.
key.lowBalance: Low balance — add credits on OpenRouter.
key.step1: Go to <link>openrouter.ai</link> and create an account (you can sign in with Google).
key.step2: In <link>Credits</link>, add credits with a card (US$ 5 is plenty).
key.step3: In Keys, click Create Key, give it a name (e.g. “Counter”) and copy the key that appears — it starts with sk-or- and is only shown in full at that moment (afterwards the list shows only the start and the end).
key.step4: Paste the key below and click “Test and save”.

errors.spaces: Paste the whole key, without spaces.
errors.incomplete: This key is incomplete. OpenRouter shows the whole key only once, when it is created — create a new key in Keys and copy it right away.
errors.rejected: This key was not accepted. Check that you copied the whole key.
errors.badResponse: OpenRouter did not answer properly (error {status}). Try again.
errors.offline: No connection to OpenRouter. Check the internet.

welcome.title: Welcome to Traffic Counter
welcome.intro: You choose the camera videos and draw the counting lines. The app finds everything that crosses the lines, an artificial intelligence suggests what each one is — and you confirm before creating the final video with the count.
welcome.prepare: Before starting, let's prepare this computer. There are 3 steps and it takes a few minutes.

gpu.title: Graphics card
gpu.text: The graphics card makes analyzing the videos much faster.

engine.title: Detection engine
engine.text: It is the program that recognizes cyclists, pedestrians and vehicles in the videos.

ai.title: Artificial intelligence
ai.text: Suggests what each object is so you only have to confirm.

welcome.engineMissing: The detection engine is not ready yet — without it the videos are not analyzed.
welcome.keyMissing: The artificial intelligence key is missing — without it there are no suggestions before the review.
welcome.finishLater: You can finish this later in Settings (at the bottom of the sidebar).
welcome.startImporting: Start by importing a video from Google Drive or from the computer.
welcome.continueWhileInstalling: You can go on while it installs

import.title: Import videos
import.intro: Each video goes through: drawing the counting lines → detecting the objects that move → a suggestion from the vision model for each one → your review → final video.
import.driveHint: Paste the link of a video or a folder (shared with “anyone with the link”).
import.computerHint: The video is used where it is, without a copy — don’t move or rename the file until it’s done.
